clusters.name: Registration Data and Input Controls
clusters.description: Captures variation in the personal data, credential fields, optional attributes, and validation controls applied during rider registration.

relations.rationale: Registration choices determine which credentials and personal attributes are available for subsequent account access and protection.

values.label: Validated personal-data registration
values.description: Collects personal registration data, including a password and optional zip code, with security and validation considerations.

clusters.name: Authentication Mechanism
clusters.description: Captures variation in the primary mechanism used to authenticate riders and establish account identity.

relations.rationale: Authentication mechanism selection depends on the credentials or identity attributes collected during registration.
Authentication mechanisms require complementary expiration and inactivity controls to limit the exposure of authenticated sessions or credentials.

values.label: Biometric thumbprint login
values.description: Uses a biometric thumbprint as the rider login mechanism.

clusters.name: Credential and Session Lifecycle
clusters.description: Captures variation in expiration and inactivity policies that limit the lifetime of verification credentials and authenticated sessions.

relations.rationale: Lifecycle controls restrict how long authentication mechanisms remain usable, reducing account exposure after compromise or inactivity.

values.label: Time-limited verification codes
values.description: Expires verification codes after 30 minutes as an authentication security control.

values.label: Inactivity-based session timeout
values.description: Automatically logs users out after 15 minutes of inactivity.

clusters.name: Sensitive Authentication Data Retention
clusters.description: Captures variation in retention and deletion treatment for sensitive authentication data, distinct from the login method itself.

relations.rationale: Data-retention decisions constrain authentication implementations by limiting how biometric artifacts may be stored and reused.

values.label: Immediate biometric-data deletion
values.description: Deletes biometric data immediately after successful authentication to support data minimization and privacy compliance.

clusters.name: Rental Operation Execution
clusters.description: Captures variation in how rental actions are represented, encapsulated, and executed within the application domain.

relations.rationale: Rental commands produce domain actions whose state changes may be propagated through event and notification mechanisms.
Rental execution is the business context in which alternative pricing policies are applied.

values.label: Command-based rental operations
values.description: Models rental operations as commands, separating action invocation from notification scheduling.

clusters.name: Event and Notification Propagation
clusters.description: Captures variation in asynchronous event propagation and user-facing notification mechanisms for bike and account state changes.

relations.rationale: Rental lifecycle actions can generate bike-state events that are asynchronously propagated to users and downstream handlers.

values.label: Observer-based user notifications
values.description: Uses the Observer pattern to notify users of bike status changes and usage-history availability.

values.label: Asynchronous bike-lifecycle events
values.description: Uses asynchronous domain events to trigger downstream bike-removal processing after bike registration.

clusters.name: Rental Pricing Policy Variation
clusters.description: Captures variation in how rental pricing rules are selected and substituted independently of notification timing or delivery.

relations.rationale: Pricing policy selection operates within rental execution but varies independently from command handling and event notification.

values.label: Strategy-based rental pricing
values.description: Uses the Strategy pattern to substitute alternative rental pricing calculations without applying that pattern to notification timing.

saturation_history.rationale: All relevant open codes are already subsumed by existing dimensions. The registration-related codes fit Dimension 1 (Registration Data and Input Controls), including personal data collection, password credentialing, optional zip code, validation, and security concerns. The biometric thumbprint and immediate deletion codes fit Dimensions 2 and 4, respectively. The 30-minute verification-code expiry and inactivity-based logout fit Dimension 3. The command-pattern and notification-scheduling separation fit Dimension 5. The observer/user-notification, bike status change event propagation, usage history notification, bike lifecycle event handling, and asynchronous bike removal codes fit Dimension 6. The strategy-based pricing calculation fits Dimension 7, and the explicit exclusion of notification timing from strategy variation does not introduce a new architectural axis; it is covered as a boundary of the pricing-vs-notification separation already present in Dimensions 5 and 7. Therefore no genuinely new concept is uncovered relative to the CityBike design space.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by existing dimensions. The session and verification-code items fit Dimensions 2 and 3 (authentication mechanism and credential/session lifecycle). The encryption and data-protection items fit Dimension 4 (sensitive data protection and retention), including protection of registration and payment data in transit and at rest. The observer-based availability updates, radius-based discovery, and real-time operational dashboard fit Dimension 6 (bike state access and propagation). The Builder-based report assembly and downloadable usage-history report align with Dimension 5 (domain operation and reporting architecture). The payment adapter/interface/normalization items fit Dimension 7 (payment integration strategy). No open code introduces a distinct architectural concern outside the existing axes, so the taxonomy is saturated for this minibatch.
